ratings.note: The browser checks write wording that the skill's own lint rejects, so most reports with routine focus, dialog, live-region or state findings fail the gate and force a hand edit of tool-generated text every time, though no reader is misled.

Every rater and verifier packet carries paths with an unstated base, so agents waste many reads and may rate or verify without ever seeing the screenshot, which weakens the evidence behind ratings in a way the report does not show.
Each fresh subagent wastes reads hunting for the schema and some give up on it, which is recurring friction that a careful agent can search past and a full path in the packet would remove.

Without a Back action the probes cannot test the classic emergency exit, so data loss on Back can only be confirmed by leaving the skill to script Playwright by hand, outside the evidence pipeline, and a less resourceful agent would miss it.

Giving heuristic evaluators the correct action path and the avoided hints breaks their independence in every run with journeys, silently inflating detection counts and biasing discoverability findings that the person trusts.

Exact-route matching cannot pair cross-role duplicates that differ only in query string or criterion, so the main deliverable repeats one problem up to six times and distorts the reader's sense of how many problems exist and which matter most.

A routine re-rate rewrites the shared blind map and the command decodes older rating files with it, silently attaching severities to the wrong findings, and only a lead who happens to notice can avoid it.

The tool knows the findings were never merged or promoted but reports only an empty queue, which the agent must investigate and could pass on as 'nothing to fix', though a careful agent or a surprised person would catch it.
Splitting needs a manual detour through hand-written candidates, a second merge and re-verification, which works on this occasional path but costs effort and puts provenance at risk.
